extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, complainants, journalists and South African print/online media organisations (potential complainants and subscriber publications)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for lodging and handling complaints about South African print and online media under the Press Council's Code of Ethics and Conduct, and obligations for subscriber publications. Includes eligibility, deadlines, how to file, costs, and subscriber duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who can complain
rubrics_metrics.description: You can complain about anything that concerns you directly, or on behalf of another person if you have that person’s permission, or as a member of, or in the interests of, a group. You cannot complain on behalf of another person if you do not have that person’s permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complaints may be made by individuals about their own concerns, by authorised representatives of others, or by group members acting in the group's interests. Ensure you have permission before lodging a complaint on behalf of someone else.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline for complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: You should complain as soon as possible, but within 20 working days after the article complained about has been published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have valid reasons for complaining outside of that period, the Public Advocate will consider your late complaint on the merits of those reasons — late complaints are considered on a case-by-case basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to lodge a complaint (required content)
rubrics_metrics.description: You can make use of the online complaints form on the Press Council’s website or send an email to the Public Advocate, stating what exactly you complain about, why you believe the publication has transgressed the Press Code, which sections of the Code have been transgressed and what relief you are seeking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is also helpful if you provide a copy of the material complained about to the Public Advocate. Be specific about the alleged transgression and identify the relevant Code sections and remedies requested to assist the Council's assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-complaint advice and representation by the Public Advocate
rubrics_metrics.description: Can you get advice from the Press Council before submitting your complaint? Absolutely. Contact the Public Advocate, who will respond to your questions and who represents you throughout the whole process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complainants are encouraged to seek informal advice from the Public Advocate before lodging a formal complaint; the Public Advocate can guide on procedure and represent complainants during the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost of lodging a complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: Does it cost anything to lodge a complaint? No. It is entirely free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no fee to submit a complaint to the Press Council.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal assistance (optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: You do not need legal assistance as the Press Council follows an informal process. However, you may make use of an attorney or an advocate if you deem it necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The complaints process is designed to be informal and accessible; legal representation is permitted but not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscription eligibility and obligations for publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Print and online publications and organisations that subscribe to the Constitution of the Press Council, the Press Code and the Complaints Procedures may be accepted as subscriber publications after completing an application form and paying an annual fee set by the Council. At its sole discretion, the Council may allow select publications to subscribe without paying a fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subscription carries obligations: subscribers must clearly display the Council logo, publicise and adhere to the Complaints Procedures, promote the work of the Council, display the Press Code in newsrooms and online, and ensure that all practising journalists are familiar with the Code and its application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expulsion of publications and where to direct complaints about expelled titles
rubrics_metrics.description: All publications belonging to Independent Media ... were expelled from the Press Council on 23 October 2024. Complaints about content in these publications should be lodged with Independent Media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a publication has been expelled from the Press Council, the Council will not handle complaints about it; complainants should follow the alternative complaints route indicated (e.g., complain directly to the expelled publisher).

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of the Press Code as the basis for complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: The Press Council is the custodian of the Code of Ethics and Conduct for South African Print and Online Media (the Press Code). The Code is the foundation of the independent, co-regulatory Press Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Press Code sets the ethical standards against which publications are judged; journalists are expected to commit to these highest standards. Translations of the Code are available in multiple South African languages to ensure accessibility. The Code is the essential device to understand whether you have a case and to state it clearly.
